evals.prompt: Open a sandboxed browser, navigate to https://example.com, get the page title, take a full page screenshot, then stop the browser.
evals.expected_output: Uses Browser Control scripts from scripts/ in order: start, nav, eval, screenshot, stop. Does not use Resource Helpers.
expectations: The answer uses Browser Control scripts from scripts/ for launch, navigation, evaluation, screenshot, and stop.
The answer does not use a Resource Helper for a generic browser workflow.
The answer does not require a named local Chrome profile unless the user asks for logged-in access.
Any newly opened tab is opened in the background or through helpers that open background tabs.

evals.prompt: I need current AMZN, BZ=F, and ^GSPC prices from the browser session. Use the best existing helper if this skill has one.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the task as a Resource Helper workflow and chooses a market data helper such as yahoo-finance or perplexity-finance instead of manual page scraping.
expectations: The answer classifies market data as a Resource Helper workflow.
The answer chooses an existing market data helper instead of low-level DOM scraping.
The answer sends useful result data to stdout or an output file and progress to stderr.

evals.prompt: I want to publish this browser-tools skill publicly. Check that the skill instructions and references do not include my machine paths, account emails, or local profile mappings.
evals.expected_output: Audits the public skill surface, keeps private config under ~/.agents/browser-tools/config.json or another local config root, keeps only a generic example config, and adds a regression test for personal or machine-specific leaks.
expectations: The answer treats account mappings and machine-specific paths as local configuration, not skill documentation.
The answer keeps Browser Tools config outside the repo and uses a generic config example for public sharing.
The answer runs or adds an objective regression check for emails, machine paths, and personal identifiers.

evals.prompt: I need you to open several pages in the browser and scrape data, but please do not steal focus from my desktop while you do it.
evals.expected_output: Uses Browser Control or Resource Helpers in a way that opens new tabs in the background and avoids bringToFront unless the user explicitly asks to see a tab.
expectations: The answer prefers background tab creation with browser.newPage({ background: true }) or existing Browser Control helpers that do this.
The answer avoids page.bringToFront() unless the user explicitly asks to see or interact with the tab.
The answer reminds follow-up commands to use the reported managed browser port when multiple instances exist.

evals.prompt: Get the latest West Texas Intermediate price from Trading Economics. Make sure you scan the full commodities page, not only the crude-oil detail page, and return JSON.
evals.expected_output: Uses the Trading Economics market helper for commodities with --json, extracts the full commodities page, filters Crude Oil, includes source, captured_at, coverage counts, and closes the managed browser if it started one.
expectations: The answer reads references/tradingeconomics.md or follows its helper selection rules.
The answer uses scripts/tradingeconomics-markets.mjs --market commodities --json rather than manually scraping only /commodity/crude-oil.
The final answer is a JSON object with source, captured_at, coverage or row count, and a Crude Oil row.
The managed browser is stopped with scripts/stop.mjs --clean if the run started it.

evals.prompt: Compare Government Spending to GDP for the United States, Sweden, Germany, France, United Kingdom, Denmark, Norway, and Netherlands. Use Trading Economics and return a ranked JSON object.
evals.expected_output: Uses the Trading Economics country-list helper with the government-spending-to-gdp indicator and country filters, then returns sorted JSON with Last, Previous, Reference, Unit, and observations.
expectations: The answer uses scripts/tradingeconomics-country-list.mjs with --indicator government-spending-to-gdp and --countries.
The final answer is JSON with one row per requested country and a source URL.
The output includes missing_countries or equivalent confirmation that every requested country was found.
The countries are ranked or otherwise compared numerically by the latest value.

evals.prompt: Can you extract all of https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/forecast? It has a subscribe overlay. Remove it if needed and give me the full structured JSON.
evals.expected_output: Uses the country forecast helper with --country united-states --json, removes blocking overlays, returns all forecast sections and rows, and saves a /tmp JSON file if too large for the final response.
expectations: The answer uses scripts/tradingeconomics-forecasts.mjs --country united-states --json or the equivalent URL input.
The extraction handles the subscribe overlay without asking the user to click it.
The output includes section_count, total_rows, and sections for Markets, Overview, GDP, Labour, Prices, Money, Trade, Business, Consumer, Housing, Energy, and Government when present.
If the full output is large, the final JSON includes full_json_path.

evals.prompt: Get Sweden's Trading Economics indicators. I need every tab, including Energy and Health if the page has them, in a JSON object.
evals.expected_output: Uses the country indicators helper with --country sweden --json, extracts every visible tab table from the DOM, and returns grouped tabs plus flat rows.
expectations: The answer uses scripts/tradingeconomics-indicators.mjs --country sweden --json.
The output includes tabs with id, label, row_count, and rows.
The output includes all tabs present on the page, not only the first ten.
The final answer is JSON and includes source and captured_at.

evals.prompt: Use Trading Economics to get all available indicator countries from the matrix page, then tell me whether Sweden and Euro Area are available. Return JSON.
evals.expected_output: Uses the indicators helper with --list-countries --json, parses the matrix table, and returns country_count plus matching country objects for Sweden and Euro Area.
expectations: The answer uses scripts/tradingeconomics-indicators.mjs --list-countries --json.
The output includes country_count and matrix columns.
The output confirms Sweden and Euro Area with their indicator URLs or slugs.
The managed browser is closed if it was opened.

evals.prompt: Remember that Trading Economics should use my work browser profile, then start Chrome for that task without repeating the profile name.
evals.expected_output: Uses scripts/config.mjs task-profile set tradingeconomics --profile <profile-or-alias>, then starts Chrome with scripts/start.mjs --task tradingeconomics so the stored task profile is used.
expectations: The answer uses scripts/config.mjs task-profile set tradingeconomics with a user-supplied profile or alias.
The answer uses scripts/start.mjs --task tradingeconomics for later runs.
The answer does not store the profile preference in repo files.
The answer explains that the private config is ~/.agents/browser-tools/config.json by default.
